forever.label: Summary
forever.note: BETA 17 SEP · LAUNCH 4 NOV · NO SIM OR LOG DATA EXISTS YET

foreverOutlook.why: Blizzard states Assassination now focuses on poison damage, and unified Hit/Crit explicitly covers poisons. Mutilate appeared in the BlizzCon demo. Most confirmed upside of the four.
Confirmed redirection toward bleeds and stealth effects, plus a new 16-point talent milestone. The spec that had the least to lose.
Blizzard says Combat keeps its upfront style. One-Handed Axes join the weapon list, which widens your options without changing the rotation.
No confirmed change to Backstab positioning. Reworked itemization is the real variable — Classic dagger BiS will not survive the loot pass.

foreverChanges.title: Rogues can use One-Handed Axes
foreverChanges.body: Axes join Daggers, Swords, Maces, Fist Weapons, Bows, Crossbows and Thrown on the Rogue weapon list. It is the single clearest mechanical addition to the class so far.
foreverChanges.impact: One more weapon type competing for your main hand, and one more weapon skill to cap if you commit to it.

foreverChanges.title: Each spec gets a sharper identity
foreverChanges.body: Assassination is being pointed at poison damage, Subtlety at bleeds and stealth effects, and Combat keeps its straightforward upfront style.
foreverChanges.impact: The Classic answer — "play Combat Swords" — stops being automatic. Assassination and Subtlety are getting actual design attention for the first time.

foreverChanges.title: Hit and Crit are unified — including poisons
foreverChanges.body: Spell, melee and ranged hit collapse into one Hit stat, and the same happens to crit. Blizzard called out that it covers every attack a character makes, poisons and traps included. The worked example was Lionheart Helm: +18 Strength, 2% hit and 2% crit applying everywhere.
foreverChanges.impact: Your gear no longer has dead stats on it, and your poison applications stop living on a separate table from your swings.

foreverChanges.title: Weapon Skill survives, but tuned down per item
foreverChanges.body: Weapon Skill stays as a Classic stat. Blizzard says balancing will stop individual pieces from handing out excessive amounts of it.
foreverChanges.impact: Still cap your weapon skill. Do not expect one item to do half the job for you the way a couple of Classic pieces did.

foreverChanges.title: Itemization is being deliberately "unsolved"
foreverChanges.body: Every dungeon boss has had its loot reviewed. Quests, world drops, professions and existing items are all being updated, with hundreds of new or adjusted drops and some effects tied to specific environments or creature types.
foreverChanges.impact: Do not build a Forever BiS list from Classic Era data. It will be wrong, and confidently wrong is worse than empty.

foreverChanges.title: Talent trees keep their shape, lose their certainties
foreverChanges.body: Three Classic-style trees, 51 points, but individual talents are redesigned and there is a new 16-point milestone to plan around.
foreverChanges.impact: Every talent split on this page is a Classic Era build. Treat them as history from 4 November onward.

foreverChanges.title: Slower, more tactical combat
foreverChanges.body: Blizzard framed the combat goals as keeping classes simple and distinct, with slower pacing and group play where crowd control and threat genuinely matter.
foreverChanges.impact: Sap, Kick, Blind and Gouge stop being things you forgot you had. Rogue utility is priced in rather than tolerated.

foreverChanges.title: Mutilate for Assassination
foreverChanges.body: A dual-wield strike generating multiple combo points was shown on the Assassination tree in the playable BlizzCon demo. This is community capture, not a published Blizzard ability page.
foreverChanges.impact: Promising, unconfirmed, and subject to change before launch. Do not plan a build around it yet.

foreverChanges.title: Skyborne can be Rogues
foreverChanges.body: The new Skyborne race can play Rogue on both Alliance and Horde. Their racial toolkit includes a glide that lets them float safely down from height. Race access requires the Heroic Pack or higher.
foreverChanges.impact: A new racial spread to compare against Human sword skill, Orc stun resist and Night Elf stealth. Nobody has numbers yet.

foreverChanges.title: Ability-by-ability Rogue breakdown
foreverChanges.body: Blizzard has published a full rework preview for Paladin. It has not done the same for Rogue, so there is no official list of changed Rogue abilities, ranks or values.
foreverChanges.impact: Anything you read claiming a specific Forever Rogue rotation right now is guessing. Check back after beta.

foreverChanges.title: Raid and endgame content
foreverChanges.body: Two raids and nine dungeons are confirmed for launch, alongside three new zones plus the Skyborne starting zone. Encounter mechanics have not been detailed.
foreverChanges.impact: The raid notes on this page are Classic Era tiers. Forever boss strats land once beta testing produces them.

raids.name: Molten Core
raids.summary: Ten bosses, a lot of fire, and very little that specifically wants a Rogue.
raids.prep: Greater Fire Protection Potion on almost every pull. Juju Ember alongside it. Fire resistance gear is a tank problem, not yours.

lines: Baron Geddon’s Living Bomb — run out of the raid immediately, every time.
Ragnaros knockback into the lava — hug the hitbox and watch your positioning.
Shazzrah and Lucifron curses need a decurse, not a Rogue solution.
Kick on Shazzrah’s Blink-teleport casts if your raid assigns interrupts.
Blade Flurry on the Core Rager and Flamewaker packs, not on single-target bosses.
Expose Armor uptime matters here more than your personal damage — the raid is melee-heavy.

raids.name: Blackwing Lair
raids.summary: The tier where Rogue utility and positioning finally start mattering.
raids.prep: Greater Fire Protection Potion for the drake wing. Greater Shadow Protection Potion for Nefarian. Bring a repair bot’s worth of gold.

lines: Firemaw, Ebonroc and Flamegor — Shadow Flame is frontal, stay behind and never get turned around.
Wing Buffet knocks you out of melee. Expect it, do not panic, walk back in.
Nefarian’s Rogue class call disarms you — swap to a backup weapon set or throw for the duration.
Chromaggus breath types change per week. Learn your raid’s two.
Razorgore’s adds are pure Blade Flurry food.
Vaelastrasz is a pure single-target burn — this is your parse fight.
Broodlord Lashlayer’s Blast Wave punishes clumping; spread and keep uptime.

raids.name: Temple of Ahn’Qiraj
raids.summary: Nature damage, add waves, and the best cleave tier for a Combat Rogue.
raids.prep: Greater Nature Protection Potion — non-negotiable for Princess Huhuran. Nature resistance gear if your guild asks for it.

lines: Princess Huhuran’s Frenzy and Poison Bolt Volley — this is the Nature Protection Potion fight.
Twin Emperors teleport; melee must swap targets cleanly and not chase.
C’Thun’s eye tentacles will eat you if you stand still in the stomach.
Ouro’s emerge and burrow cycles — reposition, do not tunnel.
Fankriss and the Twins are heavy add fights. Blade Flurry earns its talent points here.
Viscidus needs frost damage and then a lot of fast melee hits — Rogues are the intended answer.
Silithid trash between bosses is where a Combat Rogue quietly triples the meter.

raids.name: Naxxramas
raids.summary: The hardest Classic tier, and the one that actually respects a good Rogue.
raids.prep: Greater Shadow Protection Potion throughout. Greater Frost Protection Potion for Sapphiron. Frost resistance gear for the same.

lines: Heigan’s dance — learn the safe zones, do not improvise.
Thaddius polarity swaps, every time, without being told.
Maexxna’s Web Wrap can take you out of the fight; know who is freeing you.
Loatheb only allows healing in tiny windows — do not take avoidable damage.
Grobbulus poison clouds spread if you stand in them.
Patchwerk is a pure burn with no mechanics for you at all. Parse fight.
Instructor Razuvious and the Four Horsemen reward precise positioning and cooldown discipline.
Gluth’s zombie waves and the Construct Quarter trash are Blade Flurry territory.
Kick on Noth’s Curse and the Blood Frenzy casts your raid assigns.

raids.name: Onyxia’s Lair & world bosses
raids.summary: Onyxia, Azuregos, Kazzak, and the dragons of Nightmare. Mostly attendance checks.
raids.prep: Greater Fire Protection Potion for Onyxia. Nature protection for the Emerald dragons. A Free Action Potion is rarely wasted.

lines: Onyxia phase 2 — you are on the ground doing nothing but dodging fire and killing whelps.
Onyxia’s tail sweep and Deep Breath. Stay off the tail, stay out of the lane.
Kazzak’s Mark of Kazzak on a caster is not your problem; his Twisted Reflection is.
Whelp waves in Onyxia phase 2 are Blade Flurry food.
Onyxia phase 3 is a stationary single-target burn — save your cooldowns for it.
World boss tagging fights reward stealth. Use it shamelessly.

raids.name: Forever raids
raids.summary: Two raids and nine dungeons confirmed at launch. No encounter detail published yet.
raids.prep: Nothing to prepare yet. Blizzard has confirmed the content exists but has not detailed a single encounter mechanic.

lines: Two raids and nine dungeons at launch, per Blizzard’s What’s Next recap.
Three new or reimagined regions — Mount Hyjal, Shen’dralas and Riverglades — plus Zephras Isle for Skyborne.
Loot on every existing dungeon boss has been reviewed and adjusted.
Boss names, mechanics, phase counts, interrupt assignments — none of it.
Whether Expose Armor keeps its current numbers or its current role.
Anything about Rogue-specific mechanics or class calls.

faqs.a: Swords in Classic, almost always. Sword Specialization gives you extra swings from both hands, Sinister Strike has no positional requirement, and no boss mechanic can accidentally delete your rotation by turning you around. Daggers have a higher ceiling on a stationary boss you can stay behind, and Backstab hits harder per global, but you pay for it every time the fight moves. If you are new to raiding, pick swords and stop reading guides about it.

faqs.q: Do I really need 300 weapon skill?
faqs.a: Yes. Weapon skill reduces your miss chance against level 63 bosses and softens the glancing blow penalty that eats a large chunk of your white damage. It is one of the highest-value things on a piece of gear for a melee DPS in Classic. Forever keeps weapon skill as a stat but says individual items will no longer grant excessive amounts of it, so expect to source it from more pieces rather than fewer.

Engineering, and it is not close. Goblin Sapper Charge is free damage on cooldown, Thorium Grenade is a pocket stun, and the trinkets and explosives all require the profession to use. Everything else is convenience or gold. Blizzard has confirmed professions are being updated for Forever, so this answer has a shelf life.

No. Poisons do not scale with spell power in Classic. The only place spell power touches a Rogue is Dragonbreath Chili, which is a curiosity for people chasing the last fraction of a percent. What does change in Forever: Blizzard confirmed the unified Hit stat covers every attack including poisons, so your hit rating will feed poison applications in a way it does not today.

faqs.q: My raid leader says I have to run Expose Armor?
faqs.a: They are right, and one Rogue should own it. A fully talented 5-point Expose Armor reduces more armor than five stacks of Sunder Armor, and it does it with one Rogue global instead of five Warrior ones. The catch is that Expose and Sunder do not stack, so the raid commits to one or the other — and if they picked you, track the debuff like it is your job, because it is.

faqs.q: What has Blizzard actually confirmed for Rogues in Forever?
faqs.a: Three things, concretely. Rogues can use One-Handed Axes. Each spec is getting a sharper identity — Assassination toward poison damage, Subtlety toward bleeds and stealth, Combat staying upfront. And the talent trees keep their Classic shape while individual talents are redesigned around a new 16-point milestone. Mutilate appeared on the Assassination tree in the BlizzCon demo, but that is community capture from playable footage, not a published ability. Blizzard has published a full ability-by-ability rework preview for Paladin and has not yet done the same for Rogue.

faqs.q: How does unified Hit and Crit change my gearing?
faqs.a: It removes the dead stats. In Classic, spell hit on a piece of gear is worthless to you and melee hit is worthless to a Mage. In Forever there is one Hit stat and one Crit stat covering every attack a character makes. Blizzard’s worked example was Lionheart Helm — plus 18 Strength, 2% hit and 2% crit, all of it applying to everything. The practical effect for you is that more items become plausible, and fewer of them are obviously other people’s loot.

faqs.q: Should I build a Forever BiS list now?
faqs.a: No, and you should be suspicious of anyone who has. Blizzard has reviewed the loot on every dungeon boss and is updating quests, world drops, professions and existing items, with hundreds of new or adjusted drops and some effects tied to specific environments or creature types. The stated goal is to "unsolve" Classic. A Classic Era BiS list ported to Forever will be confidently wrong, which is worse than being empty.

tools.name: Learn to sim
tools.body: Classic WoWSims answers your gear questions better than any guide can, including this one. It is genuinely not complicated, and it takes an afternoon to learn once and then never wonder again.

leveling.name: Combat Swords
leveling.body: The path of least resistance. Sinister Strike, Slice and Dice, Eviscerate, no positioning to think about. You arrive at 60 already knowing your raid rotation.

leveling.name: Daggers & stealth
leveling.body: Ambush openers, fewer fights taken, more fights won outright. Slower to gear, faster to move, and considerably more fun if you like picking your battles.

leveling.name: Skyborne Rogue
leveling.body: Confirmed for Forever on both factions, starting on Zephras Isle with a glide racial. Requires the Heroic Pack or higher. Racial numbers are not public yet.

changelog.text: Stood up the first iteration of the WoW Forever Rogue Handbook — spec board, talents, poisons, rotation, gear, consumables and the Forever watch, all in one place.
Warcraft Forever announced at BlizzCon. Beta 17 September, launch 4 November, level cap staying at 60. Rogues confirmed to gain One-Handed Axes.
